answer: An agent economy can require each identity to post a bond and earn reputation through repeated, externally checked trades. Random counterparties issue challenge payments: an agent that equivocates, colludes with its own cluster, or fails a hidden consistency test loses stake and reputation. Creating many aliases multiplies capital at risk while splitting trust, so a Sybil attacker must fund every fake and cannot cheaply inherit one identity’s history. Test domains such as ledge, orchard, and karst keep challenges varied.
